findings.issue_text: app/models/optimized_image.rb:149 — Second `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts)` silently overrides the 4-arg `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` defined at line 145, so any existing caller passing width/height ints gets `height` bound as `opts` and crashes (`Integer#[]` with Symbol raises TypeError) or is misinterpreted.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — Any logged-in user can now force up to 5 sequential ImageMagick `convert` + ImageOptim runs on a 10MB attacker-controlled file inside the web process (Scheduler::Defer runs in-process) where previously oversized files were rejected before any processing; a decompression bomb (tiny PNG/JPEG decoding to gigapixels) or many concurrent uploads pins CPU/memory and DoSes the upload endpoint.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — FileHelper.is_image?` is extension-based only, so a crafted MVG/MSL/SVG polyglot renamed to `.png` reaches `convert` unvalidated (ImageMagick sniffs magic bytes, ignoring extension), exposing ImageTragick-style delegate/coder exploits to every authenticated user simply by making the file exceed max_image_size_kb.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — Return value of `OptimizedImage.downsize` is ignored and its rescue swallows all errors, so on failure the loop just re-runs the same failing convert 5 times with no logging beyond a generic message, and a partially written in-place output (from == to, truncated on crash/OOM-kill mid-write) is then persisted by `Upload.create_for` since the truncated size may now be under the limit.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — With `allow_animated_thumbnails` on and a `.gif` tempfile, the animated path invokes `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%`, which is not a valid pixel WxH for gifsicle, so every attempt fails and large animated GIFs are still rejected; with the setting off, `convert from[0]` silently flattens a large animated GIF to a single frame and stores the destroyed image without telling the user.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — SVG passes `is_image?` but ImageMagick writing back to a `.svg` path emits a rasterized/base64-embedded SVG (or fails with delegate errors), so oversized SVG uploads are silently corrupted in place rather than rejected or preserved.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — API URL download cap raised from `max_image_size_kb` to a hard 10MB for any URL and any `type` (including attachments), ignoring both size settings and widening the existing SSRF/large-fetch surface for API keys with no per-site admin control.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — Client hard-codes 10MB for every upload type (including attachments), so users with `max_attachment_size_kb` below 10MB now spend the full upload only to be rejected server-side, and the 413 message reports 10MB even when the web server's limit differs.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — Loop condition relies on `Tempfile#size` (fstat on the still-open fd) reflecting an external process rewriting the same path; this holds only because convert/gifsicle truncate in place rather than write-and-rename, so any future switch or a `to` path with a rename step makes the loop spin 5 times on a stale size and then upload the original oversized file.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — Client-side size check replaces the per-type `max_<type>_size_kb` setting with a hard-coded 10MB, so `max_attachment_size_kb` (and any admin-configured image cap) is no longer honored client-side; server still rejects, and the alert reports a limit the server does not use.

app/models/optimized_image.rb:149 — self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts)` silently overrides the 4-arg `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` defined 4 lines earlier, so any external/plugin caller passing width and height separately now has `max_height` bound to `opts` (NoMethodError on `opts[:allow_animation]` for Integer or wrong dimensions); the 4-arg version is dead code and should be removed or renamed.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — API URL-download cap changed from admin-configured `max_image_size_kb` to a fixed 10MB, and applies to non-image types too, so `max_attachment_size_kb` no longer bounds remote downloads and API clients get a different contract than the setting advertises.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:246 — 413 handler now always tells the user the limit is 10MB regardless of the real nginx `client_max_body_size` or the site setting, replacing the previously setting-driven value.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — Downsizing passes `tempfile.path` (no `.gif` extension) so `allow_animation` never selects the animated instructions; `downsize_instructions` uses `#{from}[0]`, so oversize animated GIFs are silently flattened to a single frame before `Upload.create_for`.
app/models/optimized_image.rb:151 — Public helper `OptimizedImage.dimensions(width, height)` removed without deprecation; no callers remain in app/ but plugins/lib may reference it.

app/models/optimized_image.rb:149 — Second `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` silently replaces the 4-arg `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` defined just above; any existing caller passing width/height (e.g. lib/cooked_post_processor in full Discourse) now gets a width-only "-resize W" with `opts` bound to the height Integer (TypeError on `opts[:allow_animation]`) or an ArgumentError with 5 args.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:65 — Loop condition relies on `tempfile.size`, which for an open Tempfile is an fstat on the original fd; `convert_with` runs `ImageOptim#optimize_image!` which replaces the file on disk (new inode), so the size never appears to shrink, the loop always runs all 5 iterations (0.8^5 downscale) and the stale `tempfile.size` passed to `Upload.create_for` can still exceed the limit and reject the upload.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — With `allow_animated_thumbnails` enabled, animated GIFs go through `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%`, but gifsicle's --resize-fit requires WxH (percent is not accepted), so every iteration fails (returns false, ignored), the loop spins 5 times and the upload is then rejected as too large.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — With `allow_animated_thumbnails` disabled, an oversized animated GIF is rewritten in place via `convert from[0]`, permanently flattening the user's original upload to its first frame (a thumbnail-oriented option now destroys source uploads).

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — Return value of `OptimizedImage.downsize` is ignored; on convert failure the loop keeps retrying the same failing command 5 times with no logging, and an image that shrinks but stays above the limit after 5 attempts falls through to `Upload.create_for` and is rejected with the old "too large" error despite the client no longer enforcing `max_image_size_kb`.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — Client-side limit is hard-coded to 10MB for all types, so attachments (non-images) between `max_attachment_size_kb` and 10MB now pass the client check and fail server-side, and the client alert reports 10240 KB rather than the effective server limit.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — Up to 5 synchronous ImageMagick `convert` runs plus 5 ImageOptim passes (each spawning several external optimizers) on files up to 10MB execute inside the web request, blocking a Unicorn worker for tens of seconds and letting a handful of concurrent uploads saturate CPU (no background job, no timeout, no -limit memory/map for ImageMagick).

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — Animated GIFs go through resize_instructions_animated (-coalesce on every frame) up to 5 times; a 10MB multi-frame GIF expands to frames*w*h*4 bytes uncompressed in memory per pass, easily gigabytes of RAM and minutes of CPU, with gifsicle re-run after each pass.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — The return value of OptimizedImage.downsize is ignored, so if convert fails (unsupported/corrupt image, decompression bomb hitting policy limits) the loop still spawns the full 5 convert+ImageOptim attempts on the unchanged file before Upload.create_for rejects it, all of that work wasted.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — tempfile.size uses fstat on the open Rack tempfile handle; ImageOptim replaces the output via temp-file rename (new inode), so the handle can keep reporting the original size and contents, causing all 5 passes to run and the original oversized bytes to be handed to Upload.create_for.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — 80% linear per pass gives at most 0.8^10 = ~10.7x pixel reduction after 5 attempts, and byte size does not shrink proportionally (JPEG compression ratios worsen at smaller sizes, PNG/GIF far less), so many 10MB uploads with small max_image_size_kb still fail after burning all 5 passes; a single pass computing the target scale from the size ratio would do the same work once.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — Each pass re-decodes and re-encodes the image in place (JPEG generational loss, plus repeated lossy optimizer passes), so up to 5 full decode/encode cycles are paid where one would suffice, and quality degrades cumulatively.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — Downsizing runs before Upload.create_for's SHA1 dedup check, so every re-upload of an already-known large image redoes the full multi-pass convert work instead of short-circuiting on the existing upload.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — API URL downloads now always pull up to 10MB regardless of max_image_size_kb (and for non-image types), increasing per-request network and disk usage for remote fetches.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — Client-side pre-check is raised to a hard 10MB for all types including attachments, so files over max_attachment_size_kb are now fully uploaded and then rejected server-side, wasting bandwidth and worker time.

app/models/optimized_image.rb:149 — Second `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts)` silently redefines the 4-arg `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` just above it, so any existing caller passing width and height separately now gets its height Integer treated as `opts` and fails (TypeError on `opts[:allow_animation]`) or produces wrong dimensions.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — Return value of `OptimizedImage.downsize` (false on failure) is ignored; with from == to, a failed `convert`/`gifsicle` can leave the tempfile truncated or partially written (possibly 0 bytes, which exits the loop), and the corrupt file is then passed to `Upload.create_for` and stored.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — convert_with` runs the command via backticks with the bash-only `&> /dev/null`; under /bin/sh=dash this parses as `&` (background) + `> /dev/null`, so $? is always 0, the file is rewritten asynchronously, `tempfile.size` is stale, the loop spawns up to 5 concurrent converts on the same path and the upload proceeds while the file is still being written.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — Up to 5 synchronous ImageMagick/gifsicle + ImageOptim shell-outs with no timeout run inside the web request on files up to 10MB (decompression-bomb-sized images), tying up a unicorn worker for a long time or until the request is killed, leaving the tempfile in an intermediate state.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — Animated GIFs are resized in place with gifsicle reading and writing the same path (no `-b`/temp+rename), and when `allow_animated_thumbnails` is off the `convert from[0]` path silently flattens the upload to its first frame, destroying the user's animation instead of just shrinking it.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — Client-side pre-check is hardcoded to 10MB for every upload type, so attachments over `max_attachment_size_kb` (and images when the server limit is below 10MB but downsizing fails after 5 attempts) are now uploaded in full and rejected server-side with a confusing "file too large / max N KB" error after the whole transfer.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — If 5 iterations at 80% still exceed `max_image_size_kb`, the loop exits silently and `Upload.create_for` rejects the already-modified (downsized) file with the standard size error, giving the user no indication that automatic reduction was attempted and failed.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — FileHelper.download(...) rescue nil` swallows all errors (timeouts, too-large, bad URL) so `tempfile` is nil and the guard skips downsizing, but `tempfile.size` on line 73 then raises NoMethodError which is only caught by the caller as a generic failure.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — tempfile.path is now interpolated unescaped into a backtick shell command (convert_with) and is attacker-influenced: Rack names multipart tempfiles with File.extname(original_filename) and the API path builds the Tempfile prefix from params[:type], so shell metacharacters in the extension/type reach the shell.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — Server-side ImageMagick now runs on any upload whose client-supplied filename ends in an image extension; content is never sniffed, so a 10MB MVG/MSL/SVG/PS payload named .png is handed to convert (ImageTragick-class delegate exploits if policy.xml is not hardened).

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — Up to five synchronous convert invocations on attacker-controlled images up to 10MB with no -limit memory/disk/time caps enables decompression-bomb DoS (a 10MB PNG can decode to tens of GB of pixels) for any logged-in user.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — API URL download limit is hardcoded to 10MB, overriding the admin-configured max_image_size_kb and making the (pre-existing, unfiltered) URL fetch pull larger bodies from arbitrary hosts.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — Client-side limit hardcoded to 10MB for all upload types, silently ignoring max_attachment_size_kb (server must remain the enforcement point; error message now reports a misleading limit).

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — Client validation now hard-codes 10MB for every upload type (including `attachment`), silently dropping max_attachment_size_kb enforcement; no JS test covers the attachment path or the image path against a configured site setting.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — Downsize loop is untested: `Tempfile#size` on an open handle may report the stale pre-convert inode size after ImageMagick rewrites the path, so the loop can run 5 times and `Upload.create_for` receive the wrong filesize; needs a spec asserting size shrinks and the resulting Upload succeeds.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — With allow_animated_thumbnails on, animated GIFs go through `resize_instructions_animated` (gifsicle `--resize-fit 80%`), which does not accept percentages and will fail every attempt, leaving the file oversized; no test covers animated GIF downsizing.

app/models/optimized_image.rb:150 — Redefined `OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts)` overrides the 4-arg width/height form; any external caller/spec using `downsize(from, to, w, h)` now passes `h` as `opts` and raises; no spec exercises either signature after the change.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — No test for the terminal case where the image is still larger than max_image_size_kb after 5 attempts, or when `downsize` returns false (convert/ImageOptim failure); expected outcome (rejection via Upload.create_for with the correct size) is unverified.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — Untested guard paths: max_image_size_kb = 0 must skip the loop, and non-image files (attachments) must never be passed to `OptimizedImage.downsize`; no spec covers either branch.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — API URL downloads now use a fixed 10MB cap rather than max_image_size_kb; no spec verifies a URL between the site setting and 10MB is downloaded and then downsized rather than rejected.
app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:246 — 413 handler now always reports 10240 KB regardless of the real server/nginx limit; message-content assertion is untested and can be misleading.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an in-request downsizing loop in `app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb` that, for any oversized image (`tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`), will run `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` up to 5 times before `Upload.create_for(...)`. `OptimizedImage.downsize` shells out via backticks in `convert_with`, so each attempt can be an expensive ImageMagick `convert` invocation on attacker-controlled input, blocking the web process/thread. Additionally, API URL uploads now allow downloading up to `10.megabytes` regardless of `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, increasing the amount of untrusted data that can reach this repeated processing path. This is a realistic DoS/security risk introduced by the change (even if some details like “ImageOptim” aren’t shown in the diff).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new pre-processing step in `UploadsController#create_upload` that runs `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` (which shells out to ImageMagick via `convert_with`) on user-supplied uploads when `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` is true and the tempfile exceeds `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`. This gate is based on `filename` (not content sniffing/MIME verification), so if `is_image?` is extension-driven (as the finding asserts), a non-image payload renamed with an image extension could be fed into ImageMagick, creating a potential security issue introduced/exposed by this change.

adjudication.rationale: The new loop in `uploads_controller.rb` repeatedly calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)` in-place and ignores its boolean return value. In `optimized_image.rb`, `convert_with` suppresses command output (redirects to `/dev/null`) and returns `false` on failure rather than raising, so failures are effectively silent. Because `attempt` is decremented regardless, the code will retry up to 5 times without detecting failure, and since `from == to`, a failed/partial in-place write could leave a truncated file that is then passed to `Upload.create_for` based on the (possibly reduced) `tempfile.size`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:246 — 413 handler now always tells the user the limit is 10MB regardless of the real nginx `client_max_body_size` or the site setting, replacing the previously setting-driven value.

This makes the user-facing error message always claim a 10MB limit regardless of the configured site setting (and regardless of any server-side limit), so the finding is directly supported by the change and represents incorrect behavior/feedback.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — Downsizing passes `tempfile.path` (no `.gif` extension) so `allow_animation` never selects the animated instructions; `downsize_instructions` uses `#{from}[0]`, so oversize animated GIFs are silently flattened to a single frame before `Upload.create_for`.

In `OptimizedImage.optimize`, the animated branch is selected only when `opts[:allow_animation]` is true **and** `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`. Tempfile paths typically have no `.gif` extension, so the `_animated` instructions will not be used even for GIF uploads, contrary to the intent of `allow_animation:`. The claimed specific flattening via `"#{from}[0]"` isn’t shown in the diff, but the failure to ever select animated instructions from this call site is directly supported by the diff and can lead to losing animation during resizing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/optimized_image.rb:151 — Public helper `OptimizedImage.dimensions(width, height)` removed without deprecation; no callers remain in app/ but plugins/lib may reference it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the public class method `OptimizedImage.dimensions(width, height)` (and stops using it internally), replacing it with callers passing a preformatted "WxH" string to `optimize`. While core call sites shown are updated, the diff provides no deprecation/alias for `dimensions`, so any external callers (e.g., plugins) could break. This is a compatibility concern grounded in the removal shown, though plugin usage cannot be verified from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/optimized_image.rb:149 — Second `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` silently replaces the 4-arg `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` defined just above; any existing caller passing width/height (e.g. lib/cooked_post_processor in full Discourse) now gets a width-only "-resize W" with `opts` bound to the height Integer (TypeError on `opts[:allow_animation]`) or an ArgumentError with 5 args.

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/optimized_image.rb, the diff defines `self.downsize` twice: first as `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})`, then later as `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. In Ruby, the later method definition replaces the earlier one, so any existing callers using the 4-arg (width,height) form will now either raise `ArgumentError` if passing 5 args (including opts), or mis-bind `opts` to the height Integer when passing 4 args, leading to failure when `opts[:allow_animation]` is evaluated in `optimize`. This is a concrete behavior break introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:65 — Loop condition relies on `tempfile.size`, which for an open Tempfile is an fstat on the original fd; `convert_with` runs `ImageOptim#optimize_image!` which replaces the file on disk (new inode), so the size never appears to shrink, the loop always runs all 5 iterations (0.8^5 downscale) and the stale `tempfile.size` passed to `Upload.create_for` can still exceed the limit and reject the upload.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims `convert_with` runs `ImageOptim#optimize_image!` and that it replaces the file inode, but the diff shows `OptimizedImage.convert_with` simply executes a shell command built from `*_instructions` via backticks (`` `#{instructions.join(" ")} &> /dev/null` ``) and contains no `ImageOptim` call. While `tempfile.size` potentially being stale after an external overwrite is a plausible concern, the specific mechanism asserted (ImageOptim replacing the file/inode and therefore the loop always running 5 times / stale size passed to `Upload.create_for`) is not verifiable from the diff and references behavior not present.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — With `allow_animated_thumbnails` enabled, animated GIFs go through `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%`, but gifsicle's --resize-fit requires WxH (percent is not accepted), so every iteration fails (returns false, ignored), the loop spins 5 times and the upload is then rejected as too large.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — With `allow_animated_thumbnails` disabled, an oversized animated GIF is rewritten in place via `convert from[0]`, permanently flattening the user's original upload to its first frame (a thumbnail-oriented option now destroys source uploads).

adjudication.rationale: The new upload downsizing logic rewrites the file in place (`OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)`). In `OptimizedImage.optimize`, the animated-specific path is only used when `opts[:allow_animation]` is true and the filename matches `.GIF` (`method_name += "_animated" if ...`). Therefore, when `SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` is false, an animated GIF upload will be processed via the non-animated downsize instructions, and because it overwrites the same tempfile, this can permanently strip animation/flatten the upload. The diff doesn’t show the exact `from[0]` syntax, but it does show the setting-controlled choice of animated vs non-animated processing applied to the source upload.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — Return value of `OptimizedImage.downsize` is ignored; on convert failure the loop keeps retrying the same failing command 5 times with no logging, and an image that shrinks but stays above the limit after 5 attempts falls through to `Upload.create_for` and is rejected with the old "too large" error despite the client no longer enforcing `max_image_size_kb`.

adjudication.rationale: In `uploads_controller.rb`, the new loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` without checking its return value. From the diff, `OptimizedImage.convert_with` returns `false` on failure (non-zero exitstatus) and otherwise returns `nil`, so a failed convert will leave `tempfile.size` unchanged and the loop will retry the same likely-failing command up to 5 times with no logging or early abort. After 5 attempts, the code falls through to `Upload.create_for(...)` even if the file is still over `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, so the upload will likely be rejected by downstream validations (not shown here) despite the client-side limit now being hardcoded to 10MB in `utilities.js`. This is a real robustness/UX issue introduced by the change, but it does not clearly create incorrect acceptance or data corruption on its own.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — Client-side limit is hard-coded to 10MB for all types, so attachments (non-images) between `max_attachment_size_kb` and 10MB now pass the client check and fail server-side, and the client alert reports 10240 KB rather than the effective server limit.

adjudication.rationale: In `utilities.js` the upload size check changed from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` to a hard-coded `10 * 1024` (10MB) for all upload `type`s, and the 413 handler changed from `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` to the same constant. From the diff, server-side limits are still governed by `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` / other per-type settings (no corresponding server change for non-images), so files larger than the configured limit but <= 10MB can pass the client check, then be rejected server-side, and the client-facing “max_size_kb” message will incorrectly report 10240 KB instead of the configured setting.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — Up to 5 synchronous ImageMagick `convert` runs plus 5 ImageOptim passes (each spawning several external optimizers) on files up to 10MB execute inside the web request, blocking a Unicorn worker for tens of seconds and letting a handful of concurrent uploads saturate CPU (no background job, no timeout, no -limit memory/map for ImageMagick).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a synchronous loop in `UploadsController#create_upload` that can run up to 5 times per request: `while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` calling `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)`. `OptimizedImage.downsize/optimize` executes an external command via backticks in `convert_with`, with no timeout/limits shown in the diff. This is a concrete performance/availability concern introduced by the change (blocking a Unicorn worker). However, the finding’s mention of “5 ImageOptim passes” is not evidenced in this diff; only repeated ImageMagick/convert-style calls are directly shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — Animated GIFs go through resize_instructions_animated (-coalesce on every frame) up to 5 times; a 10MB multi-frame GIF expands to frames*w*h*4 bytes uncompressed in memory per pass, easily gigabytes of RAM and minutes of CPU, with gifsicle re-run after each pass.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a loop in `uploads_controller.rb` that can call `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` up to 5 times on oversized images (`while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`). If `allow_animated_thumbnails` is enabled and the upload is a GIF, `OptimizedImage.optimize` will select the `*_instructions_animated` path (`method_name += "_animated" if ... from =~ /\.GIF$/i`), so animated GIFs can indeed be repeatedly reprocessed. However, the finding specifically claims `resize_instructions_animated` and `-coalesce` behavior and large in-memory expansion; those details are not shown in this diff (the loop uses the "downsize" operation and the contents of `*_instructions_animated` aren’t visible here). The grounded issue is the potentially expensive repeated animated processing/DoS surface, but the exact mechanism described can’t be fully verified from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — The return value of OptimizedImage.downsize is ignored, so if convert fails (unsupported/corrupt image, decompression bomb hitting policy limits) the loop still spawns the full 5 convert+ImageOptim attempts on the unchanged file before Upload.create_for rejects it, all of that work wasted.

adjudication.rationale: In uploads_controller.rb a new loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` while `tempfile.size` remains the only loop condition. In optimized_image.rb, `convert_with` returns `false` on failure and otherwise returns `nil` (no explicit success value). Since the controller ignores the return value, a failed convert won’t stop the loop; the file size stays unchanged so the loop can run up to 5 times doing repeated convert attempts before proceeding to `Upload.create_for`. This is a concrete inefficiency/perf concern introduced by the diff, but not necessarily a functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — tempfile.size uses fstat on the open Rack tempfile handle; ImageOptim replaces the output via temp-file rename (new inode), so the handle can keep reporting the original size and contents, causing all 5 passes to run and the original oversized bytes to be handed to Upload.create_for.
matched_golden_ids: The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same underlying problem: the loop relies on `tempfile.size` from an open handle, but the file is modified/replaced externally (e.g., via rename/new inode), so the reported size can be stale. This can prevent the loop from terminating as intended or cause incorrect handling (e.g., continuing passes and using the original oversized data).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — 80% linear per pass gives at most 0.8^10 = ~10.7x pixel reduction after 5 attempts, and byte size does not shrink proportionally (JPEG compression ratios worsen at smaller sizes, PNG/GIF far less), so many 10MB uploads with small max_image_size_kb still fail after burning all 5 passes; a single pass computing the target scale from the size ratio would do the same work once.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a fixed-step downsize loop in `uploads_controller.rb` that repeatedly applies `OptimizedImage.downsize(..., "80%", ...)` up to 5 times while `tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`. Because the reduction factor is constant and attempt-limited, it’s plausible (and consistent with the code) that some oversized images will still exceed the configured max after 5 passes and thus still fail later, making this a performance/robustness concern rather than a definite correctness defect. The suggestion to compute a target scale from the size ratio is a reasonable improvement grounded in the new logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — Each pass re-decodes and re-encodes the image in place (JPEG generational loss, plus repeated lossy optimizer passes), so up to 5 full decode/encode cycles are paid where one would suffice, and quality degrades cumulatively.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a loop in `create_upload` that repeatedly calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` while `tempfile.size` exceeds `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` (up to 5 iterations). Because it writes back to the same file each pass, this can indeed perform multiple decode/encode cycles on the already-recompressed output, which plausibly increases CPU cost and can cumulatively degrade quality for lossy formats. This is a concrete, diff-grounded performance/quality concern, but not a clear functional correctness defect given the intent is to shrink oversized images and multiple passes may be needed to reach the size threshold.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — Downsizing runs before Upload.create_for's SHA1 dedup check, so every re-upload of an already-known large image redoes the full multi-pass convert work instead of short-circuiting on the existing upload.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a multi-pass downsizing loop in `create_upload` that runs unconditionally (for images over the size limit) before calling `Upload.create_for(...)`. If `Upload.create_for` performs any dedup/short-circuiting based on file contents (as the finding suggests), this change would indeed force the expensive `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` work to happen before any such early-exit can occur, creating a potential performance regression on re-uploads. However, the existence/details of the SHA1 dedup check are not shown in the diff, so the claim can’t be fully verified from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — API URL downloads now always pull up to 10MB regardless of max_image_size_kb (and for non-image types), increasing per-request network and disk usage for remote fetches.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes API URL fetching from `FileHelper.download(url, SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes, ...)` to a hardcoded `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)`, so remote fetches no longer respect the configured `max_image_size_kb`. This can increase network/disk usage per request (up to 10MB) and bypasses the prior setting-based limit for any `type` passed into `create_upload`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — Client-side pre-check is raised to a hard 10MB for all types including attachments, so files over max_attachment_size_kb are now fully uploaded and then rejected server-side, wasting bandwidth and worker time.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the client-side size check in `utilities.js` from a per-type site setting (`Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`) to a hard-coded `10 * 1024` KB for all upload types. This means attachments (and any type with a lower configured limit, e.g. `max_attachment_size_kb`) can pass the client pre-check and be uploaded, only to be rejected server-side, wasting bandwidth/time. The finding matches the shown change at ~line 182.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/optimized_image.rb:149 — Second `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts)` silently redefines the 4-arg `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` just above it, so any existing caller passing width and height separately now gets its height Integer treated as `opts` and fails (TypeError on `opts[:allow_animation]`) or produces wrong dimensions.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/optimized_image.rb`, a new `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` is added after the existing `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})`. Ruby does not overload methods by arity; the latter definition replaces the former. As a result, any existing caller still passing `from, to, max_width, max_height` (no opts) will bind `dimensions = max_width` and `opts = max_height` (an Integer), and `optimize` then does `opts[:allow_animation]`, which will raise (or otherwise misbehave). This is a concrete behavior break introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — Return value of `OptimizedImage.downsize` (false on failure) is ignored; with from == to, a failed `convert`/`gifsicle` can leave the tempfile truncated or partially written (possibly 0 bytes, which exits the loop), and the corrupt file is then passed to `Upload.create_for` and stored.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an in-place downsize loop in `UploadsController#create_upload` that calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` and then proceeds to `Upload.create_for` regardless of success. In `OptimizedImage`, `convert_with` returns `false` on failure (and `nil` on success), but that return value is ignored, so a failed downsize attempt will not abort or restore the original file. Because the operation is explicitly from==to (same path), a failed external conversion could leave the tempfile in a bad state (e.g., partially written or otherwise corrupted) yet still be uploaded. The diff provides enough to verify the ignored failure path; the exact truncation-to-0-bytes scenario is plausible but not fully provable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — convert_with` runs the command via backticks with the bash-only `&> /dev/null`; under /bin/sh=dash this parses as `&` (background) + `> /dev/null`, so $? is always 0, the file is rewritten asynchronously, `tempfile.size` is stale, the loop spawns up to 5 concurrent converts on the same path and the upload proceeds while the file is still being written.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a loop in `uploads_controller.rb` that repeatedly calls `OptimizedImage.downsize` on the same `tempfile.path` until `tempfile.size` is under the limit (up to 5 attempts). `OptimizedImage.convert_with` executes the command via backticks with `&> /dev/null`, which is a bashism; when `/bin/sh` is not bash (e.g., dash), this can be parsed as backgrounding (`&`) plus redirect, causing the convert to run asynchronously while the shell returns success immediately. In that case, `tempfile.size` will remain stale inside the loop, potentially spawning multiple concurrent conversions on the same file and proceeding to `Upload.create_for` while the file is still being rewritten. This problematic interaction is directly triggered by the newly added loop logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — Up to 5 synchronous ImageMagick/gifsicle + ImageOptim shell-outs with no timeout run inside the web request on files up to 10MB (decompression-bomb-sized images), tying up a unicorn worker for a long time or until the request is killed, leaving the tempfile in an intermediate state.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds synchronous image downsizing inside the upload web request (uploads_controller.rb: new while loop with up to 5 iterations calling OptimizedImage.downsize on the tempfile). OptimizedImage.convert_with executes external commands via backticks with no timeout, so a single request can trigger multiple ImageMagick/gifsicle/ImageOptim shell-outs and tie up a unicorn worker. The resize is done in-place (tempfile.path as both input/output), so if the request/worker is killed mid-processing the tempfile can be left partially written. The diff also raises client/download limits to 10MB, increasing worst-case work per request.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — Animated GIFs are resized in place with gifsicle reading and writing the same path (no `-b`/temp+rename), and when `allow_animated_thumbnails` is off the `convert from[0]` path silently flattens the upload to its first frame, destroying the user's animation instead of just shrinking it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show in-place downsizing (`OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)`) and that GIFs only use the `_animated` pipeline when `allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` is true, but the finding’s specific claims (that the animated path uses gifsicle without `-b`/temp+rename, and that the non-animated path uses `convert from[0]` and flattens animation) are not verifiable from the shown changes because the implementations of `downsize_instructions`, `downsize_instructions_animated`, and any `convert`/gifsicle invocation details are not included in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — Client-side pre-check is hardcoded to 10MB for every upload type, so attachments over `max_attachment_size_kb` (and images when the server limit is below 10MB but downsizing fails after 5 attempts) are now uploaded in full and rejected server-side with a confusing "file too large / max N KB" error after the whole transfer.

adjudication.rationale: The diff hardcodes `maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024` in `utilities.js` for the client-side size pre-check (both the general check and the 413 handler), replacing the previous per-type `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` / `max_image_size_kb`. This means the client will no longer block uploads that exceed server-configured limits (e.g., attachments above `max_attachment_size_kb` or images when server `max_image_size_kb` is <10MB), leading to full uploads that can still be rejected server-side after transfer. The finding’s described mismatch is directly supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — If 5 iterations at 80% still exceed `max_image_size_kb`, the loop exits silently and `Upload.create_for` rejects the already-modified (downsized) file with the standard size error, giving the user no indication that automatic reduction was attempted and failed.

adjudication.rationale: The new loop in `uploads_controller.rb` (attempting up to 5 `OptimizedImage.downsize(..., "80%")` passes) does not record or surface whether downsizing was attempted or whether it succeeded. After the loop, the code always proceeds to `Upload.create_for(...)`. If the tempfile remains larger than `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`, any rejection/error will come from `Upload.create_for` with the normal “file too large” message, with no indication that automatic reduction was tried and failed. This is a real, diff-grounded UX/edge-case issue, but not a clear correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — FileHelper.download(...) rescue nil` swallows all errors (timeouts, too-large, bad URL) so `tempfile` is nil and the guard skips downsizing, but `tempfile.size` on line 73 then raises NoMethodError which is only caught by the caller as a generic failure.

The new downsizing block is guarded with `if tempfile && ...`, but immediately after, the code calls `Upload.create_for(..., tempfile, filename, tempfile.size, ...)`, which will raise `NoMethodError` when `tempfile` is nil. This follows directly from the diff and makes the rescue-to-nil behavior unsafe.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — tempfile.path is now interpolated unescaped into a backtick shell command (convert_with) and is attacker-influenced: Rack names multipart tempfiles with File.extname(original_filename) and the API path builds the Tempfile prefix from params[:type], so shell metacharacters in the extension/type reach the shell.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new loop in uploads_controller.rb that calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)` on user-supplied uploads / downloaded files. `OptimizedImage.convert_with` executes a backtick shell command built from `instructions.join(" ")`, and the `from`/`to` paths are part of those instructions (passed through `optimize` into `*_instructions`). This introduces a new code path where a tempfile path derived from untrusted inputs (notably the API download prefix uses `"discourse-upload-#{type}"`) is fed into a shell command without any visible escaping in this diff, creating a plausible command-injection risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — Server-side ImageMagick now runs on any upload whose client-supplied filename ends in an image extension; content is never sniffed, so a 10MB MVG/MSL/SVG/PS payload named .png is handed to convert (ImageTragick-class delegate exploits if policy.xml is not hardened).

adjudication.rationale: The new logic in `uploads_controller.rb` runs `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, ...)` (which shells out to ImageMagick via `convert_with`) purely gated by `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)`. In this diff, that check is based on the client-provided `filename` (no server-side MIME sniffing or magic-byte validation is shown before invoking ImageMagick). This means an attacker can supply a non-image payload with an image-looking filename and have it processed by ImageMagick, which is a security risk (ImageMagick delegate/ImageTragick-class issues) introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — Up to five synchronous convert invocations on attacker-controlled images up to 10MB with no -limit memory/disk/time caps enables decompression-bomb DoS (a 10MB PNG can decode to tens of GB of pixels) for any logged-in user.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a synchronous loop in `UploadsController#create_upload` that may invoke `OptimizedImage.downsize` up to 5 times on a user-supplied image whenever `tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` (new code around lines 66-72). `OptimizedImage` ultimately runs an external convert command via backticks in `convert_with` with no resource/time limiting shown in this diff, so repeatedly processing attacker-controlled images (now allowed up to 10MB per the new hardcoded limits) can plausibly enable CPU/memory exhaustion (e.g., decompression bomb) during upload handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — API URL download limit is hardcoded to 10MB, overriding the admin-configured max_image_size_kb and making the (pre-existing, unfiltered) URL fetch pull larger bodies from arbitrary hosts.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the API URL download size limit in `create_upload` from the admin-configured `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to a hardcoded `10.megabytes` (`uploads_controller.rb` line ~55). This demonstrably overrides the configured maximum and can increase the amount of data fetched from arbitrary URLs when the setting is below 10MB, which is a real behavior/security regression grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — Client-side limit hardcoded to 10MB for all upload types, silently ignoring max_attachment_size_kb (server must remain the enforcement point; error message now reports a misleading limit).

adjudication.rationale: The diff hardcodes `maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024` in `utilities.js` for both the pre-upload size check (`max_' + type + '_size_kb` was previously used) and the 413 handler (`Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` was previously used). This ignores per-type/max settings and can wrongly block uploads that the server would allow (if settings > 10MB) or show a misleading 10MB limit when the server is configured lower/higher, causing incorrect client behavior and inaccurate error messaging.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — Client validation now hard-codes 10MB for every upload type (including `attachment`), silently dropping max_attachment_size_kb enforcement; no JS test covers the attachment path or the image path against a configured site setting.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — Downsize loop is untested: `Tempfile#size` on an open handle may report the stale pre-convert inode size after ImageMagick rewrites the path, so the loop can run 5 times and `Upload.create_for` receive the wrong filesize; needs a spec asserting size shrinks and the resulting Upload succeeds.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a downsize loop in `uploads_controller.rb` that repeatedly checks `tempfile.size` while running `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)`, i.e., an external ImageMagick conversion that may rewrite/replace the file at the same path. Because `tempfile` is an open handle, its `#size`/stat could plausibly stay tied to the original inode/descriptor after an external rewrite, leading to extra iterations and/or passing a stale `tempfile.size` into `Upload.create_for(...)`. The diff does not refresh/reopen the Tempfile or re-stat by path, and there are no tests added around this new behavior, so a spec guarding “size shrinks and upload succeeds” is a concrete, diff-grounded request. However, the exact inode/size behavior depends on how the convert command writes the output, so it’s not 100% verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/optimized_image.rb:150 — Redefined `OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts)` overrides the 4-arg width/height form; any external caller/spec using `downsize(from, to, w, h)` now passes `h` as `opts` and raises; no spec exercises either signature after the change.
